title: Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) — Step-Up Savings Strategy
text: Save More Tomorrow (SMarT) is a behavioural finance strategy developed by economists Richard Thaler and Shlomo Benartzi (2004). The core idea: instead of committing to save a large amount immediately (which feels painful), you pre-commit to increasing your savings rate gradually — specifically, every time your income increases. How it works for Indian earners: (1) Start with a savings rate you are comfortable with today — even 5–10% of take-home pay. (2) Commit to increasing that rate by 1–2 percentage points every 6 months or at every salary hike. (3) Because raises typically happen before the step-up, you never feel the reduction in take-home pay. Research results: In the original US study, participants who used SMarT increased their savings rates from 3.5% to 11.6% over 3.5 years without feeling deprived. For Indian context: a person earning Rs 25,000/month who starts at 10% savings and increases by 2% every 6 months will save Rs 3,000/month in year 1 and Rs 5,400/month by year 3 — almost double, without lifestyle sacrifice. This approach is particularly effective for first-job earners who are building financial habits.
